cards.text: The land is being handed out tribe by tribe, and now it's the turn of the descendants of Joseph. Their share runs from the Jordan at Jericho, up into the hill country of Bethel, and west all the way to the Sea. Friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, and these folks are getting a WHOLE hill country.

cards.question: This land is the inheritance of Joseph's two sons, ___ and ___.

cards.text: Then Ephraim's own borders get mapped out, clan by clan, past Upper Beth-horon, Janoah and Jericho, and west to the Brook of Kanah and the Sea. Ephraim even gets some cities set apart inside Manasseh's land, which is like keeping your stuff in your brother's garage forever.
Ephraim moves in, but Canaanites are already living in the city of Gezer. That's getting the keys to your new place and the last tenants are still on the couch holding the remote.

cards.question: So what does Ephraim do about the Canaanites living in Gezer?

answers.text: They do not drive them out
They drive every one of them out
They hand Gezer over to Manasseh

cards.question: True or false: The Canaanites stay in Gezer among the Ephraimites, but as forced laborers.

cards.text: Now it's Manasseh's turn, Joseph's firstborn son. Manasseh's own firstborn, Machir, already received Gilead and Bashan, and friend, wait till you hear WHY.

cards.question: Why did Machir, Manasseh's firstborn, receive Gilead and Bashan?

answers.text: Because he was a man of war
Because his clan was the largest

cards.text: So this allotment is for the rest of Manasseh's clans: Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Hepher and Shemida. Six family names, friend, one for every station in my bakery, and I'm not renaming a SINGLE one.
But in the line of Hepher, a man named Zelophehad had no sons, only daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah. So where does their share go?

cards.question: Zelophehad's daughters step up to make their case. Who do they go to?

answers.text: Eleazar the priest and Joshua and the leaders
Caleb and the elders of the tribe of Judah
Aaron the priest and the sons of Levi

cards.question: The daughters tell them the LORD commanded ___ to give them an inheritance among their brothers.
True or false: Joshua turns Zelophehad's daughters away and gives their share to their uncles.

cards.text: Then the count comes in: ten shares fall to Manasseh, plus Gilead and Bashan beyond the Jordan. Friend, I get excited when a batch comes out with TEN cookies.

cards.question: Why does Manasseh end up with ten shares on top of Gilead and Bashan?

answers.text: The daughters got shares among the sons
Machir won more land in battle
Ephraim gave up some of its land

cards.text: Now Manasseh's borders get mapped out, from Asher down to Michmethath near Shechem, on to the Brook of Kanah and the Sea, with Ephraim to the south and Manasseh to the north. Around Tappuah it gets tangled: the region is Manasseh's, but the town itself is Ephraim's, like you own the yard and your neighbor owns the house sitting in the middle of it.
Manasseh is also assigned six cities inside Issachar and Asher, including Beth-shean, Taanach and Megiddo. Big names, big plans.

cards.question: Can Manasseh move into those cities assigned to them inside Issachar and Asher?

answers.text: No because the Canaanites are determined to stay
Yes and the Canaanites leave without a fight
No because Joshua gives those cities to Asher

cards.text: Time goes by, and the Israelites grow STRONGER, flexing like a stamper with brand-new edges. So what happens to those Canaanites who wouldn't budge?

cards.question: True or false: Once they're stronger, the Israelites put the Canaanites to forced labor but don't drive them out completely.

cards.text: Then the sons of Joseph come to Joshua, and friend, they are NOT here to say thank you. They've got a question about their share.

cards.question: What do the sons of Joseph ask Joshua about their share?

answers.text: Why they got only one portion
Why their land has no springs
Why Judah got the best hills

cards.question: The sons of Joseph say they have many people because the LORD has ___ them abundantly.

cards.text: Joshua hears them out. And he's got an answer ready, in case the hill country of Ephraim really is too small for them.

cards.question: What does Joshua tell the sons of Joseph to do if the hill country is too small?

answers.text: Go clear land in the forest
Take some of Judah's hill towns

cards.text: Joshua's answer is basically: big family? Great, here's an axe. But the sons of Joseph push back: the hill country isn't enough for them, and they've got something to say about the Canaanites in the valley.

cards.question: The sons of Joseph say the Canaanites in Beth-shean and the Valley of Jezreel have iron ___.

cards.text: So Joshua turns to the house of Joseph, to Ephraim and Manasseh. He tells them, "You have many people and great strength."

cards.question: True or false: Joshua tells the house of Joseph they won't have just one allotment.
And the strong Canaanites with their iron chariots? What does Joshua tell Ephraim and Manasseh about them?

cards.text: So the hill country is theirs too: it's a forest, clear it, and its farthest limits are theirs. Friend, that's a pep talk AND a chore list in one speech.

findings.problem: Joshua shows up here for the first time, as part of an answer, and no card says who he is. Later cards (stop 1 card 13, stop 2 card 6 onward) also assume the baker knows him. A story card should introduce him simply, for example as Israel's leader, before or when he first appears.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The joke compares Manasseh's six clans to the six bakery stations and says he won't rename one. The core action is clans receiving an allotment, and the comparison only matches the number six. 'I'm not renaming a single one' needs explaining before it makes sense, so a stranger would likely say 'huh?'.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The card retells Joshua's answer from 17:15 ('big family? Great, here's an axe') and then the pushback in 17:16, but it cites only Joshua 17:16. The citation should be Joshua 17:15-16.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: This last story card tells the first part of 17:18 (the hill country is theirs, it's a forest, clear it). That comes after card 15 has already asked about the end of 17:18 (you can drive them out), so the walkthrough steps backward through the verse. Telling the forest line before card 15 would keep the passage moving forward in order.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: This two-blank card marks Ephraim right only for blank 1 and Manasseh only for blank 2, following the text's order in 16:4. Nothing on earlier cards lets the baker reason out which son comes first. A baker who knows both sons could put them in the other order and be marked wrong.
findings.question: When the two blanks hold an interchangeable pair, like two names joined by 'and', must the baker match the text's order? Or should either order count as right, or should cards like this be avoided?
